title: Legal + Procurement Final Pass: MSA/DPA, KMS Clauses

Priya to produce KMS keyflow diagram and integration notes by 2025-02-20

action_items: Jordan Lee: prepare and send MSA redline (due 2025-02-18)
Priya Nair: KMS integration diagram + privilege key flow doc (due 2025-02-20)

summary: Final procurement/legal review to align MSA/DPA redlines, KMS/HSM clauses, egress pricing and entitlements. Redwood clarified hosted vs private data paths and proposed escrow/privileged-access options. Customer requested explicit audit log SLAs and a one-week turnaround on redlines. Agreed follow-ups include redlined contracts and a technical KMS diagram.
topics: DPA data residency and access controls
SLA language for audit logs and retention
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Okay hi everyone, thanks for making time. We're aware this is the final pass for the procurement and legal folks, so quick intros — I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, with Priya from our security/SE team. 
[00:12] Marta (Cobalt Procurement): Hi Jordan, hi Priya. Marta here, thanks. We also have Eileen from legal, Ravi on security and Samir joining from eng.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Great — quick agenda, align on redlines, KMS behavior in Private deployment, SLA for audit logs, and pricing entitlements for reserved capacity. Anything else to add?
[00:31] Samir (Cobalt VP Eng): Just, uh, confirm the timeline, we need to get this into finance next week so clarity there would be great.
[00:38] Eileen (Cobalt Legal): And one ask from legal: we need to see explicit language for key custody and an indemnity carve-out for certain regulated data types.
[00:46] Jordan: Sure, we'll go clause-by-clause. Starting with the MSA, we've flagged the standard 60-day termination notice — you proposed 90?
[00:55] Eileen: Right, we prefer 90 for procurement cycles. Also the DPA section: we want a stronger clause around subprocessors and flow-down obligations.
[01:05] Jordan: Understood. On subprocessors, Redwood's position is we disclose list and provide 30 days notice before adding a subprocessor. We can commit to that in the DPA redline.
[01:16] Ravi: Quick question on data residency — when you say Private deployment, is that VPC-only or do you offer an on-prem installer? We have some customers with air-gapped needs.
[01:27] Priya: Good callout. We offer a Private deployment that can be VPC-hosted in your cloud region; we also have an on-prem package for highly regulated use but that comes with a different license. For the contract we can add a clause clarifying the deployment options and data flow.
[01:41] Marta: Okay, that helps. For KMS, we need to ensure keys are customer-managed and not exportable by Redwood. Is that supported?
[01:50] Priya: Yes, customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM are supported for Private. We'll clarify the operational boundary: Redwood will never hold unencrypted primary data keys. There is an exception for ephemeral session keys used for interconnect, and we'll document that.
[02:05] Samir: Can we see the exact key rotation and backup process? We need to map to our SOC2 audit.
[02:12] Priya: We'll produce a KMS keyflow diagram showing rotation, backup, and who has privilege — we usually recommend a split KMS model for high-assurance customers. We'll include expected rotation intervals.
[02:26] Eileen: Another legal point: escrow. We'd like source-escrow for an exit scenario with 180 days notice. Is that on the table?
[02:35] Jordan: Source escrow is something we can discuss at enterprise contract level. We do have standard escrow partners, and for certain reserved capacity deals we can include escrow terms. I'll flag that to commercial.
[02:46] Marta: On SLAs — latency and availability are in commercial terms, but for audit logs we need retention guarantees and guaranteed export formats for e-discovery.
[02:57] Priya: For audit logs we can commit to X days retention on-hosted and longer for Dedicated with add-on retention. We need to capture export formats — currently CSV/JSON with timestamped entries, but we can produce NDJSON for bulk exports.
[03:12] Ravi: Also want to ensure logs are tamper-evident — checksum or signed log approach. Do you support an append-only log or at least immutability assurances?
[03:21] Priya: We don't provide a blockchain log, but we do provide signed log chains and can push log exports to customer-owned S3 buckets with object lock enabled. We'll add the exact mechanisms to the security pack.
[03:35] Jordan: Pricing path — Marta, you mentioned procurement needs a committed reserved capacity price for finance. We proposed a 12-month reserved pool with a tiered discount. Any blockers?
[03:45] Marta: The ask is the discount needs to be firm for 12 months and we need an early-exit fee schedule spelled out. Also we need clarity on overage billing and data egress fees.
[03:56] Jordan: We can commit to fixed pricing for 12 months with an early termination schedule. For egress fees, we charge per-GB for hosted, and for Private deployments we typically pass through cloud egress + a fixed per-request fee; we'll put exact rates in the SOW.
[04:12] Eileen: Please add a clause for data deletion verification — we require a signed certificate of destruction upon contract end for certain PII classes.
[04:21] Priya: We can provide a data destruction certificate for retained backups and test that within our operational runbook. We'll include evidence procedures in the security addendum.
[04:33] Samir: A technical concern — the KV cache behavior was referred to in your docs as "KV cash" in one place, it's confusing. How is session data cached across replicas?
[04:44] Priya: Sorry about the typo in the doc, that should be KV cache. Session cache is replicated to local GPU node replicas for low-latency, and persisted to encrypted blob store for warm starts. We'll add clearer language and a diagram.
[04:58] Marta: On subprocessors list — we need a list today for three items: monitoring, CDN, and backup. Can you send that?
[05:06] Jordan: Yes, we'll send the current subprocessor list as of today and commit to 30-day notice for additions.
[05:12] Eileen: What about indemnity caps — your standard MSA lists a cap equal to fees paid in 12 months. For us, given regulated workloads, we'd like a higher cap for breaches involving sensitive data.
[05:24] Jordan: We typically negotiate higher caps at enterprise level. We can propose a compromise: a higher cap for security incidents tied to SOC2 failures or confirmed data exfiltration. We'll draft language in the redline.
[05:36] Ravi: On SSO and SCIM provisioning: can we push groups and role mappings? We need SCIM sync into our idp with group mappings.
[05:44] Priya: Yes, SCIM v2 is supported. We'll include SCIM endpoints and an example mapping in the integration notes.
[05:52] Samir: For the performance check — if we go Dedicated, how long is the provisioning lead time? We need a guaranteed provisioning window for go-live planning.
[06:01] Jordan: Provisioning for Dedicated is typically 2-3 weeks after contract signature, subject to capacity. We can include a provisioning SLA in the SOW with an option to pay for expedited setup.
[06:12] Marta: Ok that's helpful. On supporting documents — we'll need the security pack, SOC2 report, penetration test summary. Can you share links?
[06:21] Priya: We'll share the security pack and an anonymized SOC2 summary today; full SOC2 report requires an NDA, which we can circulate. Link to security pack: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (note: sample link).
[06:35] Eileen: For DPA exceptions, we have two non-negotiables: explicit processing location and restriction on international transfers without adequate safeguards.
[06:45] Jordan: We'll add geography-specific processing controls and standard SCC language. For transfers, we can commit to following your data transfer rules and provide subprocessors that are within permitted jurisdictions.
[06:58] Ravi: Two quick technical asks: 1) can we run an e2e smoke test from our region to measure latencies? 2) can you provide a short-term bench of model variant for lower-cost inference?
[07:08] Priya: Yes to both — we can provide a 48-hour smoke test token pool and recommend a quantized model variant for cost-sensitive queries. We'll provide a suggested prompt set and metrics collection template.
[07:21] Jordan: Great. Let's capture next steps — we'll aim to send redlined MSA and DPA by Tuesday the 18th, Priya will send KMS diagram by Thursday the 20th, and we'll schedule a 30-min pricing check week of Feb 24th.
[07:36] Marta: That timeline works for procurement, pending Eileen's legal review.
[07:42] Eileen: Yes I'll try to return our exceptions list by Monday the 17th.
[07:47] Samir: If we can get the smoke test tokens early that'd be great — we can run basic load and latency tests.
[07:53] Priya: We'll provision a small smoke pool and send credentials to Samir.
[08:00] Jordan: Anything else? If not, thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and post the redlines into the shared drive.
[08:07] Marta: Thanks, appreciate it.
[08:10] Eileen: Thanks all.
[08:13] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: there are a few places where words were mis-transcribed (e.g. "K-V cash" instead of "KV cache") — corrected comments appear in parentheses, but the verbatim transcription preserved many filler words and interrupted sentences as-is. Links shared in-chat: security pack and SOW template (short links sent after call)."
